learn.hook: Right now, while you are reading this, the ground under you is spinning! That spinning gives us day and night.
points: The Earth is shaped like a ball (a sphere). It spins on an imaginary line called its axis. This spinning is called rotation.
The Earth takes about 24 hours to spin once. That makes one day and one night.
The half of the Earth facing the Sun has day. The half facing away from the Sun has night.
Because the Earth spins from west to east, the Sun seems to rise in the east and set in the west.
Shadows are long in the morning and evening, and shortest around noon when the Sun is high in the sky.

example.q: In a dark room, Rahul's teacher shines a torch on a globe and turns it slowly. Think it through: what does this show?
steps: The torch is like the Sun.
Only the side of the globe facing the torch is lit: that side has day.
As the globe turns, places move from light to dark: day changes to night.
example.answer: The spinning Earth gives day to the side facing the Sun and night to the other side.

learn.reallife: Arunachal Pradesh, in the far east of India, sees the sunrise before Gujarat in the far west. That is because the Earth spins from west to east.

items: The Earth spins once in about 24 hours.
One full spin gives one day and one night.
The Sun goes around the Earth to make day and night.

The Sun seems to rise in the east.
Because the Earth spins from west to east.

quiz.q: Why do we have day and night?
options: The Earth spins on its axis
The Sun switches off at night
The Moon covers the Sun every evening
Clouds block the Sun at night
quiz.explain: As the Earth spins, each place turns towards the Sun (day) and then away from it (night).
steps: The Earth spins on its axis.
The side facing the Sun has day; the other has night.
Answer: The Earth spins on its axis
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Sun moves around the Earth or switches off

quiz.q: How long does the Earth take to spin once on its axis?
quiz.explain: One spin takes about 24 hours, which is one day and one night together.
steps: One spin of the Earth takes about 24 hours.
Answer: About 24 hours
quiz.mistake: Mixes up one spin with one trip around the Sun

quiz.q: The spinning of the Earth on its axis is called
quiz.explain: Spinning on the axis is rotation. Going around the Sun is revolution.
steps: Spinning on the axis is rotation.
Going around the Sun is revolution.
Answer: rotation
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rotation and revolution

quiz.q: In which direction does the Sun rise?
quiz.explain: The Sun rises in the east and sets in the west, because the Earth spins from west to east.
steps: The Earth spins from west to east.
So the Sun seems to rise in the east.
Answer: East
quiz.mistake: Mixes up east and west

quiz.q: When is your shadow the shortest on a sunny day?
quiz.explain: At noon the Sun is high overhead, so shadows are short.
steps: Shadows are shortest when the Sun is high.
The Sun is highest around noon.
Answer: Around noon
quiz.mistake: Thinks shadows are shortest in the morning

quiz.q: What shape is the Earth?
quiz.explain: The Earth is round like a ball. Photos from space show this.
steps: The Earth is shaped like a ball (a sphere).
Answer: Like a ball (a sphere)
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Earth is flat because the ground looks flat

quiz.q: Which part of India sees the sunrise first?
quiz.explain: The Earth spins from west to east, so places in the east turn towards the Sun first.
steps: The Earth spins from west to east.
So places in the east turn towards the Sun first.
Arunachal Pradesh is in the far east of India.
Answer: Arunachal Pradesh in the east
quiz.mistake: Thinks the Sun rises at the same time everywhere

quiz.q: When it is noon in India, what is it like on the opposite side of the Earth?
quiz.explain: The side of the Earth facing away from the Sun has night.
steps: At noon India faces the Sun.
The opposite side faces away from the Sun, so it has night.
Answer: It is night there
quiz.mistake: Thinks the whole Earth has day at the same time

teach.ask: Gappu yawns: 'Where does the Sun go at night? Does it fall asleep too?'
teach.praise: So the Sun doesn't sleep! The Earth spins, and my side turns away from the Sun at night. Good night!
teach.nudge: Does the Sun really go away? What is the Earth doing that makes night come?

revise.summary: The Earth is shaped like a ball and spins on its axis (rotation) once in about 24 hours, giving day and night. Because it spins west to east, the Sun seems to rise in the east.
focus: Day and night on opposite sides of the Earth
remember: Rotation = spinning on the axis, about 24 hours
The half facing the Sun has day; the other half has night
Sun rises in the east, sets in the west
traps: Don't mix up rotation (spinning) with revolution (going around the Sun).
The Sun does not switch off at night.

learn.hook: Mangoes in summer, rain in the monsoon, warm sweaters in winter: nature repeats its patterns every year like a song with a beat!
points: The Earth goes around the Sun. This is called revolution. One trip takes about 365 days, which is one year.
The Earth's axis is tilted. Because of this tilt, different places get different amounts of sunlight during the year, and we get seasons.
In India we have summer, the monsoon (rainy season), autumn, winter and spring. Traditional Indian calendars name six seasons, called ritus.
The Moon seems to change shape. From one new moon (amavasya) to the next full moon (purnima) takes about 15 days, and the whole cycle takes about a month.
Plants follow cycles too. Many trees shed leaves and grow new ones every year. The Neelakurinji flower of the Western Ghats blooms only once in 12 years!

example.q: A year usually has 365 days, but almost every fourth year has 366 days. Think it through: why?
steps: The Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to go around the Sun.
Four quarters add up to one whole day.
So every four years, one extra day (29 February) is added.
example.answer: To add up the extra quarter days; that year is a leap year.

learn.reallife: Many Indian festivals follow nature's rhythm: Diwali falls on a new moon night, Holi near a full moon, and harvest festivals in spring and winter.

quiz.q: About how many days does the Earth take to go around the Sun once?
quiz.explain: One trip around the Sun takes about 365 days (365 and a quarter), which is one year.
steps: One trip of the Earth around the Sun takes about 365 days.
Answer: 365
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a year with a day or a month

quiz.q: The Earth moving around the Sun is called
quiz.explain: Going around the Sun is revolution. Spinning on the axis is rotation.
steps: Going around the Sun is revolution.
Answer: revolution
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rotation and revolution

quiz.q: Why do we have seasons?
options: The Sun switches off in winter
The Earth's axis is tilted as it goes around the Sun
quiz.explain: Because of the tilt, each place gets more sunlight at some times of the year and less at others.
steps: The Earth's axis is tilted.
So places get different amounts of sunlight during the year.
Answer: The Earth's axis is tilted as it goes around the Sun
quiz.mistake: Thinks seasons happen for no reason or because of the Moon

quiz.q: How many days are there in a leap year?
quiz.explain: A leap year has one extra day, 29 February, so it has 366 days.
steps: A leap year adds one extra day, 29 February.
Answer: 366
quiz.mistake: Forgets the extra day

quiz.q: How often does the Neelakurinji flower bloom?
quiz.explain: Neelakurinji covers the hills of the Western Ghats in blue only once in 12 years.
steps: Neelakurinji of the Western Ghats blooms only once in 12 years.
Answer: Once in 12 years
quiz.mistake: Thinks all flowers bloom every year

quiz.q: The night when we cannot see the Moon at all is called
quiz.explain: On a new moon night the Moon's lit side faces away from us, so we cannot see it.
steps: On a new moon (amavasya) night we cannot see the Moon.
Answer: new moon (amavasya)
quiz.mistake: Mixes up new moon and full moon

quiz.q: Which season in India brings most of the year's rain?
quiz.explain: The monsoon brings most of India's rain, mostly from June to September.
steps: The monsoon is the rainy season.
It brings most of India's rain.
Answer: Monsoon
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the rainy season with others

quiz.q: Which ritu is the season of spring?
quiz.explain: Vasant ritu is spring. Shishir is winter, Varsha is the rains and Grishma is summer.
steps: The six ritus include Vasant, Grishma, Varsha and Shishir.
Vasant is spring.
Answer: Vasant
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the names of the ritus

teach.ask: Gappu shivers, then sweats: 'Why is it cold in December and hot in May? Do seasons come back every year?'
teach.praise: I see! The tilted Earth goes around the Sun in a year, so the seasons come back again and again!
teach.nudge: How long does the Earth take to go around the Sun? And what makes seasons happen?

revise.summary: The Earth goes around the Sun (revolution) once in about 365 days. Its tilted axis gives us seasons. The Moon and plants also follow cycles.
remember: Revolution ≈ 365 days = one year; leap year = 366 days
Seasons come from the tilt of the Earth's axis
India: summer, monsoon, autumn, winter, spring; Vasant = spring
traps: Seasons are not caused by the Sun switching off or clouds.

learn.hook: Every winter, thousands of birds fly over the Himalayas to visit India, and some come all the way from Central Asia and Siberia. Why do they make such long trips?
points: Migration is when animals travel far from one place to another at a certain time of the year, and later return.
Animals migrate to find food, to escape the cold, or to lay eggs and raise their young.
Amur falcons stop in Nagaland every October–November on their long journey to Africa. Bar-headed geese fly over the Himalayas to spend the winter in India.
Flamingos raise their chicks in the Rann of Kutch. Demoiselle cranes spend winter in Khichan village, Rajasthan.

Olive Ridley sea turtles come in huge numbers to lay eggs on Odisha's beaches. Some herders, like the Gaddis of Himachal Pradesh, move with their flocks to the hills in summer and back down in winter.

example.q: In winter, many lakes in Siberia freeze over. Think it through: why do some birds from there fly to India in winter?
steps: Frozen lakes mean birds cannot find fish, insects or plants to eat.
India is warmer in winter, and its lakes and wetlands have food.
So the birds fly to India for the winter and go back in spring.
example.answer: They come to find food and warmth, and go back when the cold ends.

learn.reallife: In winter, visit Keoladeo National Park in Bharatpur or Chilika Lake in Odisha to watch migratory birds. Dr Salim Ali, the 'Birdman of India', studied many such birds.

revise.summary: Migration is when animals travel far at a certain time of year and later return, to find food, escape cold or lay eggs. India sees Amur falcons, bar-headed geese, flamingos, demoiselle cranes and Olive Ridley turtles.
focus: Meaning of migration and its reasons
Migrating animals and the places they visit
Herders who move with the seasons
remember: Bar-headed geese fly over the Himalayas; flamingos raise chicks in the Rann of Kutch
Demoiselle cranes winter in Khichan, Rajasthan; Olive Ridley turtles lay eggs in Odisha
Gaddis take flocks up the hills in summer; Salim Ali = Birdman of India
traps: Migration is not sleeping all winter.
Gaddis go up to the hills in summer, not winter.
